_notes: NEXT-SHAPE fleet config (ADR-0031: runner pool and job queue). Equivalent to fleet.json as of
2026-08-23 — same 7 streams — but lanes no longer own accounts. This file is NOT read by the
running supervisor: the code that understands it ships in the same commit, and a supervisor
started before that commit keeps its last good config and complains if it sees this shape.
At the next drain window the operator renames this file over fleet.json and restarts the
fleet service (docs/OPERATIONS.md, 'Switching to the pool/queue shape'). The new code also
loads the OLD shape, so either file works after the restart.
accounts.pinned: account -> lane name. A pinned lane is exactly today's lane: one lane, one
account, its own roster stream, enabled/drain/respawn semantics unchanged. The lanes list
holds ONLY pinned lanes; every lane there must appear in accounts.pinned.
accounts.pool: the accounts the queue may use, in preference order. Whenever one is free
(no job on it, not held live per the roster's own account-busy inference) the supervisor
takes the next runnable job from `queue` and spawns it there. Never PROBE, never SMOKE*.
roster: named entries, the exact per-entry schema of roster JSONs plus `tiers` — the
episode tiers the model has been PROMOTED into (ADR-0030). Default ["e90"]. Promotion is
a recorded operator/eval decision: edit tiers here, never expect the supervisor to compute
it. No entry carries an account: the pool assigns one.
queue: ordered jobs { ref, episode, repeat, lane?, enabled? }. `ref` is a roster name or a
list of them (a list rotates several models on one account exactly as a multi-entry lane
does today). `episode` is e90 | e360 | freeplay, passed to the runner as --episode <id>
with the equivalent explicit watchdog flags alongside (e360: 360 min wall clock, idle 20m,
no-xp off, maxToolCalls 2000; freeplay: no wall clock, unscored). `repeat` is a count or
"loop" (run-roster --loop). `lane` names the job's run ids and logs
(fleet-<lane>-<model>-<stamp>); default <first ref>-<episode>. A job whose episode is not in
a ref's tiers runs without that ref; a job with no promoted ref is SKIPPED with a logged
reason and --status shows it. A model already running under one job is not started under
another (one stream per model). A loop job holds its pool account until it is disabled or
removed; with 6 pool accounts the first 6 runnable loop jobs are the fleet and the rest
wait in order — reorder or disable to rotate. Disabling a running job drains it at the
next episode boundary, same as a lane. A job that exits stays finished until it is
disabled and re-enabled (rearm), same as a lane.
Lane policy is unchanged and enforced on every entry: claude models only via the
claude-subscription driver; shared free pools carry free ids only; a local apiBase is
exempt from the suffix rule. preflight is unchanged (ADR-0023); its accounts may not be
in the pool.
e360 jobs for sonnet and qwen3.8-27b are present but DISABLED: enabling one is the
promotion step — first add "e360" to that roster entry's tiers, then flip enabled. Until
the tiers edit the job is skipped with a reason, by design.
